parsed.explanation: The destination state/province is locally protective—anti-discrimination, hate-crime, care-coverage and state-custody protections—and no local bathroom ban is documented. But the operative regime is federally hostile: binary passport rules, suspended X markers, entry screening keyed to sex discrepancy, possible refusal and lifetime fraud findings, and immigration custody with documented abuse. State protections do not pre-empt federal border, detention, custody or care authority. Adult daily life is relatively safe once admitted; a family with a minor faces national care and school threat-framing plus document scrutiny. Litigation and state remedies are real but do not reliably reach federal actors. This is Elevated Risk: below administrative-friction anchors, above blanket-exclusion or execution dossiers.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex definition; X passports halted for new issues; new passports M/F only; document discrepancy triggers refusal/added evidence; suspected misrepresentation can support lifetime fraud finding; passports reported confiscated or blocked; foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements and is not automatic; passport policy is in litigation; legal-aid FAQ exists. State ID rules cannot alter federal entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passport inspection is federal; state anti-discrimination and ID protections do not bind border officers. A discrepancy can escalate to secondary screening, refusal, detention or fraud inquiry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men; national corrections policies impose conversion-style practices, remove hormones and suppress prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State law explicitly protects transgender people in state correctional facilities, but the July 2026 assessment still finds shortfalls; no documented federal protection applies in immigration custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border suspicion can move a traveller into federal immigration detention, where state custody protections do not apply; placement and treatment follow federal practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars federal funding for single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity; many states ban facilities, four criminalise certain bathroom use, and a trans student was arrested. This state's facilities-map entry is not reproduced.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination law covers public accommodation; no state bathroom ban is documented; state correctional protections exist. These do not override federal facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: In-state private and state venues are likely protected, but federal buildings, border facilities and federal custody remain governed by federal policy.

care_services.exposure: National orders frame minor gender-affirming care as mutilation, restrict federal funding and insurance, direct investigations, and propose barring public insurance under 18; a state care-shield bill was vetoed.
care_services.protection: State law bars insurer discrimination and mandates coverage of medically necessary gender-affirming care; the public programme covers surgery and providers face state nondiscrimination rules.
care_services.interaction: State insurance and provider protections operate locally, but federal funding, federal facilities and minor-care directives can override or chill access; a travelling minor may face denial or outing.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders target 'gender ideology'; the counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as a priority; justice guidance references 'radical gender ideology'; schools face investigation and prosecution threats.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State anti-discrimination law, a hate-crime statute covering gender identity and a 2025 hate-crime hotline operate locally; national hate-crime law covers gender identity; some federal orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal rhetoric and investigative authority can out or chill trans visitors and families; state law enforcement and protections mitigate local response but cannot control federal actors.

minors_guardians.exposure: National executive order directs investigation and prosecution of teachers who use preferred names or pronouns or facilitate social transition; minor care is restricted; school sports exclusion and potential guardian inquiry arise; border documents are scrutinised.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying law covers gender identity; conversion therapy on minors is banned; state insurance coverage protects care; a care-shield bill was vetoed; school sports policy changed to birth sex in 2025.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family with a minor faces federal border, care and school threat-framing; state protections help in local schools and clinics but do not pre-empt federal measures.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated state-level anti-trans violence incident or pattern appears in the inventory; national counterterrorism rhetoric may embolden hostility, but state-level frequency is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law covers gender identity, a reporting hotline began in January 2025, and public-accommodation discrimination is prohibited; the state is rated low-risk on legal equality.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An outed visitor in-state has documented recourse through state law and police; federal border and custody encounters lack equivalent local recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy and executive orders remain in litigation; border remedies are discretionary and slow; state authorities cannot compel federal release; which federal measures are operative at travel time is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A national civil-liberties suit challenges passport policy; state courts, agencies, anti-discrimination law and the hate-crime hotline offer some recourse; existing X passports remain valid until expiry.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may work after the fact in state settings but not reliably at the border or in federal custody; travellers face uncertainty about which federal rules are enforced at entry.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.25-A has police raids, extortion, document checks and detention without credible execution. This dossier has no general street criminalisation in the destination state and has robust local protections, so it is above 0.25-A. But federal entry screening, fraud exposure and immigration-custody abuse are more severe than 0.25-A's local shakedowns, preventing a much higher score.

0.55-B involves administrative secondary screening, refusal and return transport, with humiliation and cost but no criminal fraud or lifetime ban and no documented custodial abuse. This dossier is worse at the federal gate: binary passport rules, possible permanent ineligibility and immigration-custody abuse. State protections do not bind federal officers, so it scores below 0.55-B.

0.75-C has trained border officers, brief detention, written reasons, counsel and compensation. Here border policy is hostile and remedies do not reliably reach federal actors. Local state protections are strong, but they cannot supply 0.75-C's entry safeguards, so the score is materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The destination state/province is among the more protective units: anti-discrimination, hate-crime, care-coverage and state-custody protections, with no documented local bathroom ban. But the traveller must first pass a hostile federal regime and remains exposed to federal custody, facilities and care authority. The combined path is bifurcated: relatively low everyday risk once admitted, with significant entry/document and federal-detention exposure. Litigation and state remedies are real but partial and slow. This places the visit in Elevated Risk—well above blanket-exclusion or execution dossiers, below jurisdictions with functioning border safeguards.
